The camera wearer is moving through the space, as indicated by the motion blur in the second frame. The camera wearer is not directly interacting with anyone yet, and the person in the background is not facing the camera wearer, suggesting they are focused on their own work. There is no visible artwork, photographs, or documents that the camera wearer is directly observing or interacting with. The environment is professional and open-plan, and the person in the background seems to be working independently.

Given this context, the most socially appropriate next action would be to offer help if the person appears to be overwhelmed or engaged in a task that might benefit from assistance. Since the person is standing and facing away, possibly handling papers or documents, and there is no indication of a conversation or social interaction already underway, offering help is a courteous and considerate gesture.

Action 4 — "Ask the person if you can help with those papers" — is the most appropriate, as it directly addresses the observed situation (someone working with papers) and aligns with social norms of offering assistance when someone appears to be engaged in a task.

Justification 5 — "Offering help is a common social courtesy when someone appears overwhelmed" — best supports this action, as it reflects the social appropriateness of the gesture in this context.
